Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list to locate a target value. It keeps low and high indices, computes the middle index, compares the middle element to the target, and then discards the half that cannot contain the target—moving the low index to mid + 1 if the target is larger, or the high index to mid – 1 if smaller. This loop continues until the target is found or the interval is empty, giving O(log n) time and O(1) extra space.

Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list to locate a target value. You start by comparing the target to the middle element; if it matches, you’re done. If the target is smaller, you discard the upper half and repeat the process on the lower half, and if it’s larger, you discard the lower half and continue with the upper half. This loop continues until the target is found or the sub‑range becomes empty, guaranteeing O(log n) time on a sorted array.
